subject: Business
title: The Nibble: Small Asks After Agreement
description: A quick win: understand The Nibble: Small Asks After Agreement.

hook.text: You agree on the car price. Then the buyer says: 'You'll throw in floor mats, right?' Most sellers say yes.

buildup.text: The nibble is a small, last-minute request made after the main deal is done.

discovery.text: It works because the other side is psychologically committed. Saying no to a small ask feels petty.

twist.text: Each nibble is small alone, but they add up. Repeat nibbles erode the deal's value significantly.

climax.text: The defense: 'I'd be happy to discuss that — let's reopen the full agreement.' That stops nibbles fast.

punchline.text: Small asks at the end aren't small. They're strategy.

quiz.question: Why are nibbles effective after a deal is agreed?
options: The other side is committed and reluctant to reopen the deal over a small ask
They are legally required to accept minor additions
Nibbles are only used in car sales

details.summary: The nibble is a last-minute request for small concessions after the main terms are agreed upon, exploiting the other party's desire to finalize the deal. These small asks seem insignificant individually but can add up to meaningful value when used systematically by skilled negotiators.
details.whyItMatters: Nibbles exploit the psychological commitment to closure. After investing effort in reaching agreement, people resist reopening major issues and readily concede small requests to avoid jeopardizing the deal.
takeaways: Nibbles are small last-minute requests that exploit the desire to close the deal
Individually minor, nibbles can accumulate into significant concessions over time
Recognizing the tactic lets you counter by requesting reciprocal small concessions

faq.question: How should you respond when someone nibbles after reaching an agreement?
faq.answer: Ask for something of equal value in return to establish reciprocity. Say I can do that if you can do this small thing for me. Alternatively, explain that the agreed terms were a complete package. If the nibble is truly minor, granting it can build goodwill if you set the precedent of reciprocity.

faq.question: Is it ethical to use the nibble technique?
faq.answer: Small asks after agreement are common and generally acceptable in business. The line is crossed when nibbles are planned as a strategy to extract value beyond what was fairly negotiated, or when they are so frequent they undermine trust. Use nibbles sparingly and be willing to concede them too.
